To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

photoreceptor degeneration in the rd1 mutant mouse model of retinoschisis leads to changes in the retinal microenvironment that include increased cell proliferation and migration and altered gene expression.

the rd1 mouse retina undergoes a cellular response to photoreceptor cell death that includes the up-regulation of the pro-apoptotic protein Bax and the activation of the transcription factor nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-κB).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of novel imaging techniques for the detection of early retinal changes in the rd1 and the rd10 mouse models of retinal degenerations.
the cellular and molecular mechanisms that underlie the development of the retina, and the cellular responses to degeneration in the retina.
the development of new methods for the synthesis of organic materials, and the study of their physical properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the retina is a highly complex organ, with a high degree of organization and specialization.
the retina is a complex tissue, which is highly dependent upon the presence of photoreceptors for survival and function.

there is no evidence that the rd1 mouse has a significant immune response to photoreceptor degeneration and the immune cells that are found in the rd1 retina are likely to be there as a result of the degenerative process rather than a cause of the disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that photoreceptor cell death in the rd mouse model is not associated with the activation of a cell death program.
photoreceptor death leads to a cascade of cellular responses in the outer retina, which ultimately results in a loss of retinal function.
we have identified a number of cellular responses in the rd1 retina to photoreceptor cell death.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rd1 mouse is a good model to investigate the cellular responses to photorecetor death.
the retina is a dynamic organ that responds to injury by activating a variety of cell types to promote regeneration.
there is an increase in the expression of the pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IL-6 in the rd1 retina, which is likely a response to photoreceptor cell death.
